000:1: The Foreword is a guide to the cosmic terms we need for reading the whole Urantia Book.
000:4: The Foreword of The Urantia Book does not teach one separate doctrine. It was prepared to explain in advance the key terms that will appear again and again—**God · divinity · Deity · reality · personality · energy · the Absolutes · the Trinity**.
000:5: The human language of Urantia has limits when it comes to expressing the vast realities of the universe. So the revelators tell us that they use existing human language as far as possible, and introduce new terms only when they truly must.
000:6: The most important thing in reading the Foreword is not to try to grasp every idea completely at once. It becomes much easier if we think of it as **a map showing how the whole structure of the universe relates to divine reality**.
000:11: The name of the world we live on
000:13: The local universe to which Urantia belongs
000:15: One of the seven superuniverses, the one to which Nebadon belongs
000:17: The eternal and perfect central universe at the center of the seven superuniverses
000:19: The eternal center of all universes, where God dwells
000:21: The present organized creation: Havona plus the seven superuniverses
000:23: The still larger whole that includes the grand universe and the universes of outer space
000:26: In the Foreword, **Deity** is a wider idea than God. Deity may appear personally, but it can also function in ways that are prepersonal or superpersonal.
000:27: **Divinity**, on the other hand, is the unifying and co-ordinating quality that Deity shows. We understand divinity as truth, beauty, and goodness, and in personal relationships we can experience it as love, mercy, and ministry.

000:34: Deity of possibility, with purpose and will
000:36: Deity in personal relationship and divine association
000:38: Deity that shares and reveals itself
000:40: Deity that grows with its creatures and expands itself
000:42: Deity that unifies creature and Creator experience in time and space
000:44: Deity that functions on the absonite level, beyond time and space
000:46: Deity is a broad idea that includes not only who God is but also how Deity functions.
000:49: The Foreword always links the word **God** with personality. When the context does not say otherwise, God usually means the Universal Father.
000:54: Creator · Controller · Upholder, the Universal Father
000:56: Co-ordinate Creator · Spirit Controller, the Eternal Son
000:58: Conjoint Actor · Universal Integrator · Mind Bestower, the Infinite Spirit
000:60: God as he evolves and is experienced in time and space
000:62: The seven levels of Deity manifestation that help creatures of time and space draw near to God
000:64: The experiential God of the absonite level, beyond time and space
000:66: God as he becomes experientially actual on the absolute level
000:68: The key point is that the word God is not one simple idea; it covers **the many ways personal divinity is revealed on different levels**.
000:71: The Universal Father, as the **First Source and Center**, is the source of all reality. In the end, no being and no thing can exist apart from him.
000:76: The Universal Father, source of all reality
000:82: The absolute center of material gravity and of the material reality of the universe
000:86: The balance and adjustment between deified and undeified reality
000:90: Because eternity and infinity are hard for us to understand, the Foreword uses the philosophic expression **the I AM**. It is not meant to point to some actual starting point in time; it is a way of explaining, in our time-bound human thinking, a reality that has neither beginning nor end.
000:93: Universe reality does not exist in only one form. The Foreword describes reality broadly as **deified reality, undeified reality, and the interassociated reality that links the two**.
000:98: The realm of impersonal energy and material reality
000:100: The realm of divine and spiritual reality that can be personalized
000:102: Reality that links the two realms in relationship and balance
000:104: Distinctions from the viewpoint of time and space
000:107: What has already appeared / what still exists as possibility
000:109: Levels of reality according to how far they transcend time and space
000:111: What exists from eternity / what becomes actual through experience and evolution
000:113: What exists as a person / reality that is not personal
000:115: Paradise is not a Creator personality but **the absolute center of the material reality and gravity of the universe**. That is why the Foreword does not identify Paradise with God.
000:118: Personality does not come about by itself; it is **a unique gift bestowed by the Universal Father**. Personality is not the body, the mind, the spirit, or the soul as such; it is the lasting reality that unifies all of these into one self.
000:125: The intellectual and emotional function that thinks, feels, and judges
000:127: The Thought Adjuster who indwells the human being
000:129: The morontial reality that grows through human choices and the work of the Thought Adjuster
000:131: The unique identity given by the Universal Father that unifies body, mind, spirit, and soul
000:133: Personality is not body, mind, spirit, or soul. Personality unifies them all into one person.
000:136: The Foreword uses the word energy broadly—not only for the material realm but also for the realms of spirit and mind. It also explains that the universe has circuits and centers that link each of these realms.
000:141: What responds to the personality circuit of the Father
000:143: What responds to the spirit circuit of the Son
000:145: What responds to the mind circuit of the Infinite Spirit
000:147: Energy-matter that responds to the material gravity of Paradise
000:152: Primal energy that does not yet respond even to Paradise gravity
000:154: The stage that responds to Paradise gravity but not yet to local gravity
000:156: Material energy that responds both to Paradise gravity and to linear gravity
000:158: Pattern is **the original form** that can be reproduced. Paradise is the absolute pattern, and the Eternal Son is described as the pattern personality.
000:161: The Foreword distinguishes **existential Deity** from **experiential Deity**. The Father, the Son, and the Spirit exist from eternity, but the Supreme Being is experiential Deity who becomes actual as the experience of creatures and Creators accumulates in the universes of time and space.
000:166: Deity who exists eternally—past, present, and future
000:168: Deity who becomes actual through the history of the universe and the experience of creatures
000:170: **Rather than thinking of the Supreme Being as a creator who directly makes all things, **it is easier to understand him as the being who gathers up and unifies all the experiences of creatures and Creators that take place in time and space**.**
000:173: Because it is hard for finite human beings to reach the infinite God directly, the Foreword explains that the Universal Father has provided an approach called **God the Sevenfold**, so that evolving creatures can find God step by step.
000:192: The mortal discovery of God begins with the Creator Son of our nearby local universe, gradually ascends to higher levels of divinity, and at last arrives at the recognition of the **Universal Father**.
000:195: God the Ultimate refers to a level of experiential divinity higher than the Supreme Being. If the Supreme Being mainly unifies the finite experience of the universes of time and space, **God the Ultimate is Deity becoming actual on the absonite level, which transcends time and space**.
000:196: So God the Ultimate is an idea very far from anything human beings can experience directly today. He is presented as an expression of divinity connected with the greater future development of the master universe.
000:199: Even the Foreword explains God the Absolute with great care. The term points to **divinity that will become experientially actual on the absolute level**, which lies far beyond present finite human understanding.
000:200: The Foreword itself admits that it cannot fully explain this level. So it is better to receive this part not as something to be completely understood but as **the farthest horizon of cosmic possibility**.
000:203: The Foreword explains the infinite potential of the universe through the relationship of the three Absolutes. The three are distinct in function, but in the end they are unified within one infinite whole.
000:208: Infinite potential that is divine and can be personalized
000:210: Impersonal and unqualified cosmic force and potential
000:212: The reality that adjusts and balances the tension between the Deity Absolute and the Unqualified Absolute
000:214: Behind the fact that finite and infinite, time and eternity, man and God can exist together lies the adjusting function of the Universal Absolute.
000:217: The Paradise Trinity is **the eternal Deity union of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit**. It is the existential Trinity, without beginning.
000:218: On the other hand, the Foreword explains that in the evolution of the universe, **experiential Trinities** such as the Trinity Ultimate and the Trinity Absolute are still in the process of becoming actual.
000:223: The existential Trinity that exists from eternity
000:225: The first experiential Trinity, now evolving
000:227: The second experiential Trinity, now in the process of actualization
000:229: The Trinity is not simply calling three beings by one name; it means **a real cosmic structure of divine relationship and unity**.
000:232: The revelators tell us that in writing these papers they made full use of the high philosophic and religious concepts that human beings had already discovered. Only where existing human concepts could not explain a matter did they supplement them with higher cosmic knowledge.
000:233: They also admit that it is impossible to translate eternity and divinity fully into human language. But because **the Thought Adjuster, a fragment of God,** dwells within us and **the Spirit of Truth** is at work, they say that human beings can gradually come to understand spiritual values and cosmic meanings.
000:236: The Foreword is not a chapter of answers to memorize but a concept map for reading the whole Urantia Book.
000:240: Deity is a broad cosmic idea, and divinity is its unifying quality
000:244: The Universal Father is the source of all reality
000:246: Universe reality appears as deified, undeified, and interassociated
000:248: Personality is a unique gift of the Universal Father
000:250: Energy works on many levels, and pattern is the original for reproduction
000:252: The Supreme Being evolves as he unifies the experience of time and space
000:254: The way finite creatures approach God step by step
000:256: The experiential God of the absonite level, beyond time and space
000:258: Divinity that will become actual on the absolute level
000:260: Three functional phases of infinite potential
000:262: The cosmic structure of divine relationship and unity
000:264: The Foreword of The Urantia Book takes us beyond the single familiar word God and shows how **divinity · reality · personality · the universe · the Absolutes · the Trinity** are all connected with one another.
000:265: It may feel difficult at first, but there is no need to memorize every term at once. As we read each paper afterward, we can come back to this Foreword and see where each idea belongs.
000:266: First see the whole structure → learn the terms → come back to the Foreword as you read each paper.
001:1: “Is God a person, rather than a force or a law?”
001:4: Paper 1 opens the door to the whole Urantia Book. It deals with one thing only: **who God is**.
001:5: The text gives us an order to follow. First think of God as **Creator**, then as **controller**, and last as **infinite upholder**.
001:6: But what Paper 1 stresses most is something else. God is not a vast force or a law of nature; he is **a true personality**. He is one who can know and be known, who can love and be loved.
001:7: And this personality has given us one command. It is not meant to frighten us; it is an invitation that calls us forward without end.
001:9: ⟦Q 1:0.3⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect.⟦/Q⟧
001:12: Surprisingly, **God has never revealed his own name.** He reveals himself only through his nature.
001:13: So the name a creature gives to the Creator shows exactly how that creature understands God. When we call him Father, that too is **a name we have chosen**, a name that grew as we came to realize our personal relationship with him.
001:19: Far out in the space of the universes
001:28: Father of Lights, Gift of Life, All-powerful One
001:31: Other planets of the local system
001:32: Father of Fathers, the Paradise Father, the Havona Father, the Spirit Father
001:35: Those who know him through the bestowals
001:38: Having so many names does not mean confusion. It means that the same one God has been met by each from his own place. Whatever name we use, **what matters is to know him and to long to be like him**.
001:39: There is one more thing to remember. **God does not require any recognition, formal worship, or slavish service.** The only thing we can truly give him is **the choice of our will** to do the Father’s will. That is the reality of true worship.
001:42: God is primal reality in the spirit world, the source of truth in the mind spheres, and he overshadows all throughout the material realms. Yet **God is neither manlike nor machinelike.**
001:43: Paper 1 points out, one by one, the things that God is not. This list shows us how small our ideas of God have been.
001:47: A projection of man’s highest hopes or longings
001:48: A transcendent reality, beyond the highest values that man can imagine
001:49: A synonym for nature, natural law given a human shape
001:50: Universal spirit, eternal truth, infinite reality, and father personality
001:51: An idea or potential of righteousness
001:52: The God of salvation and the Father of love
001:53: A projection of spiritual meaning made by the mind, the highest product of man
001:54: He may be all these to the human mind, but in fact he is more
001:56: How then do we know that God exists? Paper 1 answers clearly: we can know it in human experience through **the presence of the Thought Adjuster who indwells us**. That presence shows itself in three ways.
001:65: The personality’s craving to be like God, the wholehearted desire to do his will
001:67: Therefore **the existence of God can never be proved by scientific experiment or by logical deduction.** It can be realized only in the realm of human experience. Yet the true concept of God is logically reasonable, philosophically sound, and religiously essential.
001:68: One more fact should be added. The Universal Father is **not the direct creator** of our local universe; Nebadon is the creation of his Son Michael. Yet the Father still controls that universe, and through his fragmented spirit he keeps in direct contact with his children.
001:71: “God is spirit.” To say we were made in God’s image **does not mean that we look like him.** It means that Mystery Monitors sent from his presence dwell within us.
001:72: God is invisible not because he hides himself from lowly creatures. Quite the opposite. **His glory is so great and so intense that no material creature can approach it.**
001:73: But this is no reason to lose heart. **We do not need to see him with the eyes of the flesh in order to discern him.** The faith-vision of a spiritualized mind is enough.
001:74: Here Paper 1 shows us the crossroads that divides our whole life. The human mind is joined to matter and cannot of itself pass beyond death. The question is **what that mind subordinates itself to**.
001:79: Becomes more and more material and at last enters the path of personality extinction
001:81: Becomes more and more spiritual, survives, and gains eternity by becoming one with the guiding divine spirit
001:83: The Divine Counselor who presented this paper bears witness: though the great God is absolute, eternal, and infinite, **he is also good, divine, and gracious.**
001:86: Because God’s perfection is infinite, he is forever a mystery. But among all these mysteries Paper 1 singles out **the most unfathomable one**.
001:87: It is not the size of the universe or the length of eternity. It is **the fact that God dwells within the human mind**. This is the mystery of mysteries.
001:89: The physical bodies of mortals are “the temples of God.”
001:91: In the end, the divine mystery lies in the gap between two places that are very far apart. The gap looks like this.
001:106: Yet there is something God does in the face of this gap. **He reveals himself without fail to each and every creature, to the full limit of that creature’s capacity to grasp him spiritually.** ⟦Q 192:2.2⟧God is no respecter of persons.⟦/Q⟧
001:107: So how much I know God now is not a question of how much he has hidden himself, but of **how much I am able to receive**.
001:110: **This section is the heart of Paper 1. **Do not let the majesty and infinity of God obscure his personality.
001:111: “⟦Q 1:5.1⟧He who planned the ear, shall he not hear? He who formed the eye, shall he not see?⟦/Q⟧” God is infinite and at the same time personal—he is **an infinite personality**.
001:112: What happens if we deny that God is a person? Paper 1 says that only two paths are left.
001:118: When a man dies he loses his body, so his personality vanishes
001:119: It wrongly assumes that a material body is essential to personality
001:121: God has no body, so he has no personality
001:122: It repeats the same assumption from the opposite side
001:124: Both extremes come from the same error: **the idea that personality must have a material form**. But a body is not essential to personality, either in man or in God.
001:125: Personality is not simply one of God’s attributes. It stands for **the totality of the co-ordinated infinite nature and the unified divine will**, and it is the revelation of God to the universe of universes.
001:126: And this personality does not merely watch us from afar. The infinite God **takes a direct part in the ascending struggle of every imperfect soul.** That is why the following words are not a figure of speech but literally true.
001:128: ⟦Q 1:5.16⟧In all your afflictions he is afflicted.⟦/Q⟧ ⟦Q 1:5.16⟧In all your triumphs he triumphs in and with you.⟦/Q⟧
001:131: Human personality is **the time-space shadow cast by the divine Creator personality**. We cannot know the reality by staring only at the shadow; the shadow must be interpreted in the light of the true substance.
001:132: The same God looks entirely different depending on where we view him from.
001:137: A primal force, the first cause
001:141: A living spiritual experience, the loving heavenly Father
001:143: And there is something we must not forget. **God and man look at personality from opposite directions.** Man looks up from the finite toward the infinite; God looks down from the infinite upon the finite.
001:144: That is why a better concept of divine personality had to wait for a better concept of human personality to appear. There is one place where both were revealed together: **the bestowal life of Michael lived out on Urantia**.
001:145: We may argue about God. But **experience with God transcends all argument.** So the person who knows God does not use his experience as a weapon to defeat others.
001:148: When Jesus spoke of the living God, he was pointing to a personal Deity—**the Father in heaven**.
001:149: Why is personality so important? **Because between nonpersonal things there can be interaction, but not fellowship.** The relation of father and son is possible only when both are persons.
001:150: So union with God does not happen the way a drop of water dissolves and vanishes in the ocean. It comes about through **progressive spiritual communion, personal contact, and wholehearted agreement with his will**. The self does not disappear.
001:155: Can be perceived apart from personality
001:159: Is truly understood only in relation to personality — only persons can love and be loved
001:161: So even beauty and truth, **if they are not linked with the loving Father**, become unrelated to the hope of survival.
001:162: Finally, Paper 1 honestly admits that these profound truths are not fully clear even to the Paradise beings to whom the author belongs. Yet it tells us not to be discouraged, because they **will become clearer and clearer as our minds become increasingly spiritualized**.
001:169: God does not reveal his name; he reveals himself through his nature
001:171: God’s existence is known not by proof but by the presence of the indwelling spirit
001:173: He is invisible not because he hides but because his glory is so great
001:175: The deepest mystery is that God lives within the human mind
001:177: Infinity does not obscure personality — he is a true person
001:179: Human personality is the shadow cast in time by the Creator personality
001:181: Only persons can have fellowship, can love and be loved
001:183: What Paper 1 gives us is not information about God. It is **a place from which we can call upon God**.
001:184: He is not a force, a law, or an idea. He is one who can know and be known, who can love and be loved, and **who can become our friend**.
001:185: God, revealing no name, came to us through his nature → placed a fragment of himself within us → following that guidance, our minds become subservient to spirit → and at last we stand in his presence.
001:187: This is the knowable and lovable God shown to us in “The Universal Father.”
002:4: If Paper 1 told us **who** God is, Paper 2 tells us **what God is like**. It is a paper about the character of God.
002:5: The best way to understand the nature of God is not speculation. It is to understand **the life of Jesus of Nazareth**. The life that Michael of Nebadon lived as a man showed us exactly what the Father is like.
002:6: There is another way as well: to **recognize ourselves as children of God** and to look upon the Paradise Creator as our true spiritual Father. When we become sons, we see the Father.
002:7: Paper 2 looks at the character of God under seven headings: infinity, perfection, justice, mercy, love, goodness, and truth and beauty. These seven are not separate qualities; they are **seven faces of one personality**.
002:9: ⟦Q 2:5.10⟧God is love, but love is not God.⟦/Q⟧
002:12: The Father’s presence is so bright that to lowly creatures he seems to **“dwell in the thick darkness.”** He is unseen not because there is too little light but because there is too much.
002:13: God knows his own infinity and eternity fully, lacking nothing. He is **neither an accidental product of the universe nor one who experiments with it.**
002:14: **With God there is nothing new.** No cosmic event is ever a surprise to him. For God there is no past, present, or future; at any moment, all time is present to him. ⟦Q 2:1.5⟧He is the great and **only I AM**.⟦/Q⟧
002:25: Sees the end from the beginning — every experiment and adventure lies within his eternal purpose
002:27: Yet this very infinity raises a problem. **One who is absolutely infinite cannot make direct contact with finite beings.** So God opened ways to come near to us.
002:32: Perfect in divinity, yet they share the flesh and blood of the planetary races and become one of us — God becoming man
002:34: Seraphim and countless other celestial beings of mind draw near to beings of lowly origin and minister to them
002:36: A gift directly from the great God himself — he comes to dwell in our minds without announcement or explanation
002:38: In all of this the Father **lovingly and willingly steps down, modifies, and attenuates his infinity.** He makes himself less in order to come closer to us.
002:39: And yet his infinity is not diminished at all. So the words “In him we live and move and have our being” are **literally true**.
002:42: “⟦Q 2:2.1⟧I am the Lord; I change not⟦/Q⟧.” In God’s dealings there is **no variableness or shadow of changing.** His plans are steadfast, his will is immutable, and his acts are infallible.
002:43: At times God seems to change according to our attitudes. But that is **only the surface.** Beneath it his unchanging purpose and eternal plan remain just as they are.
002:44: God’s perfection does not consist in claiming to be right. It consists in **the perfection of goodness inherent in his nature**.
002:45: Here we meet a surprising statement. Because God is infinitely perfect, **he cannot know imperfection as his own personal experience.** Yet he **shares** the experience of imperfection that the struggling creatures of the evolutionary universes go through.
002:46: So my immaturity and failures are not unrelated to God. The Universal Father really **takes part in the experience of immaturity and imperfection** that appears in the evolving lives of moral beings.
002:49: God is righteous; therefore he is fair. There is no iniquity in him; **he is no respecter of persons, and he takes no bribe.**
002:50: So it is futile to plead with God to change his unchanging decrees, or to let us escape reaping what we have sown. **“Whatsoever a man sows, that shall he also reap.”**
002:51: **But here is the good news. **Even in the act of justice that reaps the harvest of wrongdoing, divine justice is always tempered by mercy.
002:52: The gravest consequence is not punishment but **the end of existence**. ⟦Q 2:3.2⟧The final result of wholehearted sin is annihilation.⟦/Q⟧ Yet even this is not God destroying anyone. By embracing iniquity, the sinner **has made himself unreal and so destroyed himself**.
002:53: **And even that extinction is not carried out at once. **It is always delayed until due process has been fully completed.
002:58: Charges are brought on the sphere where the wrongdoer lives
002:60: Planetary tribunals → courts of the Creator Son → judicial hearing of the Ancients of Days
002:62: After the charges are confirmed without interruption, the mandate comes from the high courts of the superuniverse
002:64: After confirmation from above, the judges of the superuniverse headquarters carry it out directly
002:66: The Creator Sons devote themselves to the rehabilitation of rebels and of beings fallen into error
002:69: What is mercy? Paper 2 defines it very precisely: **mercy is simply justice tempered by wisdom**—the wisdom that, with perfect knowledge, fully understands the natural weaknesses and environmental handicaps of finite creatures.
002:70: So there is no need to persuade the Father to show mercy. **The creature’s need alone is enough.** Because God knows all his children, it is easy for him to forgive.
002:71: This applies to us as well. **The better a man understands his neighbor, the easier it is to forgive him, even to love him.** Often we cannot forgive not because our hearts are hard but because we do not yet understand.
002:76: Springs from God’s righteousness and does not depend on the deeds or performance of the creature
002:78: Supreme justice adjusted to the situation of evolving finite beings
002:80: What eternal justice and divine mercy together produce in human experience
002:82: Mercy never violates justice; it is an understanding interpretation of supreme justice
002:84: God is never **the victim of emotional contradiction.** He does not waver between love and principle as we do. His infinite wisdom always knows the way to satisfy justice and mercy at the same time.
002:87: **“God is love.”** Therefore his personal attitude toward everything in the universe always shows itself as a response of divine affection.
002:88: Here there is a misunderstanding that must be corrected. **God did not come to love us because of someone’s sacrifice or intercession.** “⟦Q 2:5.2⟧The Father himself loves you⟦/Q⟧.”
002:92: Someone’s sacrifice drew out God’s love
002:93: The Father himself loves us, and in response to that love he sent the Thought Adjuster
002:94: To be forgiven we need a mediator
002:95: The affectionate heavenly Father requires no mediator to secure his favor or forgiveness
002:97: ⟦Q 2:6.7⟧God is never wrathful, vengeful, or angry⟦/Q⟧
002:98: The God of justice and the God of love are different
002:99: The Father’s personality is not divided, and his divine unity is perfect
002:101: What is the greatest proof of God’s goodness? It is **the Thought Adjuster** within us. He **waits patiently** for the time when the two of us will become one forever.
002:102: There may be days when, however hard we search, we cannot find God. That is all right. **If we simply follow the leading of the spirit within**, step by step we shall go forward until at last we stand in the Father’s presence.
002:103: Between us and God there is a gap of space and a gap of spirit. But **he has already bridged that gap in his own way.** He has sent his own spirit to dwell within us.
002:104: The author of Paper 2 confesses that even if God were not great and mighty, **so long as he is so good and merciful, I would love him just the same.** We love the Father not because of his wonderful attributes but **because of his nature**.
002:105: **And the reason is simple. **The experience of loving can only be a response to the experience of being loved.
002:108: Beauty can be seen in the physical universe, and truth can be known in the intellectual world. But **the goodness of God is found only in the spiritual realm of personal religious experience.**
002:109: So religion, in its essence, is **a faith-trust in the goodness of God**. A man may fear a great God, but **he can trust and love only a good God.**
002:110: **This is exactly what Jesus did. He lifted **the concept of God from a morality based on the authority of a king to a morality of loving care within the family intimacy of parent and child.
002:115: Set a high moral standard, but left the believer always insecure about his status in time and eternity
002:117: A concept one step further, proclaimed by the Hebrew prophets
002:119: God as revealed by Jesus — he transcendently illuminated the whole human concept of God
002:121: ⟦Q 2:6.4⟧God loves not like a father, but as a father.⟦/Q⟧
002:123: The saying “⟦Q 2:6.8⟧God loves the sinner and hates the sin⟦/Q⟧” must be understood precisely. **Personality can love or hate only another personality.** Sin is not a person, so God has no personal attitude toward sin.
002:124: **So **the love of God seeks to save the sinner, and the law of God seeks to destroy the sin.** Love and law are not at war; each is doing its own work.**
002:127: All finite knowledge is relative. Even knowledge from the highest sources is **only relatively complete, locally accurate, and personally true.**
002:128: Divine truth, final truth, is uniform and universal. But because those who pass it on differ in the depth of their knowledge and experience, **differences arise in the details.** Knowing this keeps us from becoming impatient when we meet differing testimonies.
002:129: **Here too lies the most serious mistake philosophers make: **the error of abstraction—seizing one aspect of reality and declaring it to be the whole of truth**.**
002:130: **Truth is beautiful because it is both full and symmetrical.** So the person who searches for truth is already seeking divine reality.
002:145: The greatest error of Hebrew religion was **its failure to associate the goodness of God with the truths of science and the beauty of art**. A morality that stresses goodness alone, cut off from the rest, in the end fails to win people’s devotion.
002:146: **So the way for religion to recover today is clear. Besides its moral commands, it must give equal attention to **the truths of science, philosophy, and spiritual experience, the beauties of the physical creation, the charm of intellectual art, and the grandeur of genuine character achievement**.**
002:147: When truth, beauty, and goodness come into harmony in one person’s experience, the result is **a high kind of love, tempered by wisdom and qualified by loyalty**. Health, sanity, and happiness are themselves the blending of these three in our lives.
002:150: ⟦Q 2:6.6⟧God as a father transcends God as a judge.⟦/Q⟧
